title: E4M3/E5M2 FP8 profile gating and calibration ramp for Hopper stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable and stabilize FP8 quantization profiles for Hopper-class GPUs by introducing deterministic profile gating between E4M3 and E5M2, improving calibration robustness, and adding CI-grade accuracy validation. Deliverables: (1) per-model automated selection flow that picks E4M3 or E5M2 based on calibration metrics; (2) stability fixes for infrequent NaN/overflow cases observed in long-running KV-cache workloads; (3) a gated canary rollout and rollback runbook; (4) unit+integration CI that fails on accuracy regressions beyond configurable thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Automated profile selector chooses E4M3 or E5M2 per model with documented thresholds and deterministic tie-breakers
No single-model accuracy regression >1.0% on the canonical eval suite (lm-eval + internal prompt set) compared to baseline INT8/FP16 for at least 10 models across sizes
Calibration pipeline produces stable scale/zero-point estimates across 5 independent runs (stdev < 0.5% for critical layers)
Canary deployment path validated: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> full with automated rollback on latency or accuracy regression alerts
CI integration: nightly job that runs calibration + inference on representative mini-bench and blocks merges if thresholds are exceeded
notes: Decision: prefer E4M3 for matrix-multiply-dominant transformer blocks; fall back to E5M2 for attention softmax and normalization layers where dynamic range is higher
Trade-off: E4M3 gives lower quantization noise but requires stricter overflow detection; introduced dynamic guardband that biases toward E5M2 when underflow/overflow risk increases
Calibration approach: two-stage — coarse global histogram collection followed by per-layer per-channel re-centering using clipped-moments
Stability fixes: added saturating arithmetic path for fused-kernel outputs and explicit NaN/Inf inspectors in KV cache restore code
Performance: kernel selection caches per-model profile to avoid runtime decisions on hot path; measured 3-6% throughput improvement vs naive profile switching

implementation_steps: 1) Add deterministic selector binary with config flags for thresholds and weighting factors
2) Extend calibration pipeline: histogram collection -> clipped-moments -> per-channel min/max smoothing
3) Implement saturating arithmetic path and NaN/Inf inspectors in fused kernels
4) Add CI job: calibration + eval suite + throughput smoke test
5) Canary rollout plan automation: feature-flagged ramp with monitoring hooks and automated rollback
6) Post-release: telemetry dashboards for per-model quantization deltas and overflow counters
risks_mitigation: Risk: Latency regressions when selector runs on hot path. Mitigation: cache decisions in model metadata and run selector asynchronously during warmup
Risk: Calibration non-determinism causing flakey CI. Mitigation: seed RNGs, fix sample ordering, and add deterministic mini-bench for CI
Risk: Uncaught overflow leading to silent corruption in long-lived sessions. Mitigation: runtime crash-and-rollforward policy + automatic fallback to E5M2/FP16 on detection
